The nation’s largest labor movement, the Nagkaisa Labor Coalition, also called on Filipinos to join the mobilization on EDSA on Sunday to “manifest strong people’s protest against corruption and to demand genuine accountability from those who plundered public funds.”

“The trillions of pesos poured into flood control projects and other infrastructure that went instead to senators, members of the House, DPWH officials, and their cohorts in business and the private sector is abominable. These repeated acts are shocking to conscience and must end — and end now,” the labor group said on Saturday.

Other labor groups are also taking part and made their own calls for participation.

data.text:
ACTIVISTS, RELIGIOUS GROUPS HOLD MASS VS CORRUPTION

Activists and various civil groups attend a Mass concelebrated by the Conference of Major Superiors in the Philippines (CMSP) and presided over by Fr. Marion Bayaras at the Manila Cathedral in Intramuros on Sunday, Sept. 21, as part of the “Baha sa Luneta: Aksyon na Laban sa Korapsyon” movement. 

The liturgy, held on the 53rd anniversary of the declaration of Martial Law, was followed by demonstrations in Luneta Park and Mendiola.

(Photos by Precious Kae A. Andaya/ The Varsitarian)

As of 9:15 AM, crowds start gathering at Rizal Park in Manila on Sunday for anti-corruption rallies and to mark the 53rd commemoration of martial law.

According to the Manila Public Information Office (PIO), an estimated 13,000 people have already assembled at the venue to take part in the rally. (Facebook/Manila Public Information Office)
